newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: The South African rand advanced below the 4.50 level to its strongest level in four months on Wednesday amid heavy offshore and local exporter dollar sales.

At 1425 GMT, the rand was pegged at 4.4900/4930 from 4.5265/5295 at Tuesday's close, after touching a day's best level of 4.4825 bid against the dollar -- its strongest level since September 20 last year.
Dealers said the rand had been buoyed by a flood of dollars on the day as the bullish sentiment which has helped the rand firm over 20 cents this year remained entrenched.
"It was just a lot of investment inflows and exporter interest. It was very much one-way trade today. Everybody wanted to sell dollars and it was pretty hectic," one dealer said.

Dealers said that strong rumours that the President Nelson Mandela would use his opening of Parliament speech on Friday to make a major announcement on the removal exchange controls had bolstered sentiment on the day.
"We heard strong rumours out of London and New York that there is going to be a "big bang" announcement on exchange controls," one trader said.
South African Finance Minister Trevor Manuel had no comment when asked whether there was any truth to the speculation.
"I've seen some very interesting rumours in the market," Manuel told reporters in Cape Town, declining to comment further on the matter.
Other traders felt the rumours were baseless as the rand needed to endure a period of sustained stability before government made any moves to relax the controls.
"Four weeks of rand strength is not enough to motivate any exchange control abolition," said one senior trader.
A report in the Financial Times quoting Goldman Sachs as calculating the rand's real value at around 4.18 to the dollar was also cited as a factor which enthused the market on the day.
Dealers said the rand's rally was expected to continue on Thursday although at a slower pace. They expected it to firm to 4.45 by the end of the week.
Against the crosses, the rand firmed against sterling to 7.3284/3411 versus 7.3311/3405 and was also slightly firmer against the mark at 0.3664/3667 compared to 0.3623/3626.
The rash of new Eurorand bond issues, which topped two billion rand in January and amount to 650 million rand so far in February, also continued to inspire demand, dealers said.
Jacque Mulder, chief dealer at the South African branch of ABN AMRO NV, said: "We believe the rand offers good value at this point and investors should respond accordingly."
ABN AMRO earlier issued a new 100 million rand three-year Eurorand issue, while Rabobank doubled its three-year 14.75 percent bond to 200 million rand.
On the bond market, bond yields retraced earlier losses to end lower on the back of the stronger rand and firmer U.S. Treasury bonds.
The benchmark R150 bond was yielding 15.07 percent at the local close from 15.125 percent late Tuesday.
Dealers said that while underlying sentiment remained bullish, there was some nervousness in the market ahead of Thursday's option close-out.
"The market will be driven by the option close-out tomorrow. The big picture is still bullish but it's difficult to say what's likely to happen ahead of the options close-out," one dealer said.
Dealers said also pointed to the improvement in the local business mood in December/January as a factor which would encourage continued foreign interest.
The South African Chamber of Business said on Wednesday that its business confidence index rose one percentage point to 112.3 in December/January from 111.3 in November last year.
"The higher local business confidence gives impetus to foreigners' confidence in our market," another one said.
On the money market, short-term rates were unchanged despite a higher money market shortage.
The Reserve Bank indicated the daily shortage at 9.851 billion rand on Tuesday from 9.258 billion rand on Monday.
Three-month NCDs were quoted unchanged from Tuesday's 16.60 percent offered level, while the 90-day BA rate was also steady at between 15.95 percent and 16.15 percent bid.
Foreigners bought 149.14 million rands worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after buying 60.16 million rands worth on Monday, the Bond Exchange said.
Nominal cumulative turnover on the bond market on Tuesday was 10.34 billion rand from 7.03 billion rand on Monday.
-- Emelia Sithole, Johannesburg newsroom +27 11 482 1003
